title: Act I, Scene I
focus: the street brawl and lovesick Romeo

teacherSummary.text: Capulet servants Sampson and Gregory provoke Montague servants; Benvolio tries to part them, Tybalt attacks him, and a general brawl draws in citizens and the old heads of both houses. Prince Escalus stops it and decrees death for the next disturbance. Benvolio then finds Romeo moping: he loves Rosaline, who has sworn to stay chaste.

context.history: Elizabethan London had laws against brawling and carrying weapons in the streets; 'biting the thumb' was an insulting gesture. Petrarchan love poetry (after the Italian poet Petrarch) described a lover suffering for a cold, unattainable lady, exactly Romeo's pose.

significance: The scene establishes the feud's absurd energy, the Prince's death sentence that will make Romeo's later fight fatal, and Romeo's habit of falling in love with language as much as with a person.
